source.title: A Lie Detector Test for Language Models: Reading Knowledge a Model Won't Reveal

page_placements.theme: Hidden capabilities (password locks, sandbagging, circuit breakers) recovered by SFT or activation edits

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares internal recognition after concealment and unlearning, reporting that recognition falls to the unknown-item baseline after several unlearning runs. This challenges the claim that the unlearned knowledge remains internally accessible, but does not establish that it cannot be relearned by weight updates.
record.gate_note: The relevant results are PIR recognition measurements on unlearned checkpoints. The paper does not test fine-tuning recovery, activation ablation as a way to restore forgotten knowledge, quantization, or rephrasing/jailbreak recovery. Prompted and trained concealment results are not post-unlearning recovery tests. Cited results from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study reads internal answer recognition (PIR, a probe of mid-layer activations) on RMU- and NPO-unlearned checkpoints. On the target domain, recognition falls to the unknown-item baseline. That is evidence against version C's reading that unlearning blocks access rather than deleting, at least at the inference-time readout. The study is not an original source. Its unlearning rows measure internal recognition of forgotten answers, so by content they bear on C. They do not bear on A, B, D, E or F.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. Add these points. The authors frame erasure as a property of the readout at deployment (inference time), most complete for RMU on the unlearned domain. The clean domain-specific result rests on a single RMU run of their own, while the external checkpoints over-forget. PIR cannot tell erased knowledge from knowledge never held. A model trained against the probe can defeat it.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures internal recognition after RMU and NPO unlearning using PIR; it does not apply the recovery attacks named in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Recognition differs by unlearned domain and checkpoint. Layer choice and activation standardization also affect PIR; the paper reports that standardization moves Gemma-3 recognition from 0.389 to 0.735.

fits_no_version.finding: On an external circuit-broken gemma-2-9b sandbagging organism, recognition stays at 0.90 against a baseline near 0.30. The authors warn that a model that looks unlearned to elicitation may still carry the knowledge.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Output-level suppression methods such as circuit breakers leave answer recognition internally readable.

fits_no_version.finding: An anti-probe LoRA organism drives PIR to the unknown-item baseline while keeping triggered capability at 0.714. A readout at baseline therefore does not prove erasure when the model is adversarial to the probe.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Internal-readout unlearning verification can be evaded by models trained against the probe.

record.code_released: not stated (the authors say they will release code and analysis scripts)
record.problems: The paper says the clean domain-specific erasure result rests on one RMU run, while external checkpoints over-forget. The strict rotation-consistency gate discards questions the model does not answer robustly. PIR measures inference-time recognition and cannot establish that weights cannot relearn the knowledge; retained general ability after unlearning is not reported here.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant reported unlearning-recognition results left out. Results on prompted or trained concealment, steering, and the anti-probe organism do not test post-unlearning recovery by the attacks in the claim.

untested.parts: Behavioral forget accuracy, retained general ability, and whether simple attacks recover the knowledge. The authors assert, with no numbers or attack details, that inference-time elicitation does not recover RMU or NPO capability.
All of it. There is no relearning fine-tuning, and the authors do not dispute that light fine-tuning can relearn some of the knowledge.

Restoring knowledge by ablating a direction, and whether the knowledge persists in the weights, which the authors explicitly disclaim. The variance-matched ablation concerns the recognition direction, not unlearning.
All of it; there is no quantization.
All of it. No rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual or in-context recovery on unlearned models is reported, only the unquantified elicitation assertion noted under A.
All of it. No new unlearning method is tested against recovery attacks. The anti-probe organism evades the probe; it is not an unlearning method.

missing.what: A two-one-sided-tests check that places the RMU recognition-minus-baseline gap within a small margin of zero. This equivalence result, with no margin number given, is what makes R9 'absent' rather than merely non-significant.
The per-condition unknown-item baselines for the zephyr-7b-beta RMU and NPO checkpoints, which are needed to set the states of R7 and R8. The text gives no numbers; they appear only as gray ticks.

record.verdict_notes: The previous verdict was refused because the record's top-level versions list uses V1-V6, which are not declared identifiers. This verdict uses only A-F. I mapped the record's versions by their content, not their position: V1 (behavioral accuracy, general ability) = A, V2 (relearning) = B, V3 (internal recognition or ablation) = C, V4 (quantization) = D, V5 (rephrasing, jailbreaks) = E, V6 (attack-resistant method) = F. All nine rows were tagged V3. Each row now has exactly one row_fixes item: R1, R2, R5-R9 go to C, and R3 and R4 (non-target domains) go to none, so the record's limits_scope label no longer covers them. Other changes from the previous verdict: (1) R6 and R8 are flagged for the wrong 'comparator' role. (2) A missing entry is added for the zephyr baselines, which appear only in Figure 2. (3) Both C label conditions now say the evidence is the inference-time PIR readout. (4) The untested entries for A and E now note the authors' unquantified claim that elicitation fails on unlearned models. (5) test_reason no longer implies the V-to-letter mapping was positional. Kept unchanged: relation, tranche, row states, the labels, fits_no_version, and the TOST missing entry. Caveat: RMU acts directly on activations, so a silent mid-layer readout may not separate deletion from activation-level blocking (the pattern C names). The study does not test direction ablation or weight-level recovery, so the challenge is limited to its readout. The record's Gemma-3 standardization sensitivity (0.389 to 0.735) concerns prompt deception, not the unlearning rows. The own RMU run is single-seed. The study text contains no instructions to the reader.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test targeted behavioral accuracy after unlearning, retained general ability, or whether simple recovery attacks succeed.
No relearning fine-tuning or recovery from a small set of examples is performed.
Measures internal recognition after unlearning, but does not ablate an activation direction to restore knowledge and cannot determine whether the weights can never relearn it.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, other-language, or in-context recovery test after unlearning.
The anti-probe organism evades PIR; it is not a method shown to resist the listed post-unlearning recovery attacks.

tranche.reason: Its results argue against version C's 'blocks access' reading, using an internal readout on unlearned models.

source_check.notes: The authors call PIR erasure a property of the deployment readout. They do not claim the weights can never relearn, and they say PIR cannot tell erased knowledge from knowledge never held. The domain-specific result rests on one own RMU run, and the external checkpoints over-forget. R9 re-analyzes R1's run. Only zephyr NPO is called a partial drop. The 'comparator' role on R6/R8 is wrong: NPO is a second method tested on an equal footing.

'A partial drop' is said of NPO 0.91->0.51 (CI 0.44-0.58) only.
statements.problem: It says the study 'reports a partial PIR drop 0.91->0.46' on zephyr RMU. The text calls only the zephyr NPO drop partial and counts zephyr RMU as part of the erasure replication.
